correctness.rationale: Smoothness over the entire algebraic closure follows from the coordinate-value quadratic equation and exhaustive multiplicity cases, not an F3 search; empty F3 set follows exactly from nonzero-coordinate counts. The generic Bring curve is Q-isogenous to E50a^4 by Braden–Disney-Hogg Proposition 4.5; good reduction therefore transports its l-adic Frobenius characteristic polynomial. Zero points yields a3=1 and the all-extension zeta. Actual standalone polynomial and finite-field checks independently confirm the Cartier identity and first two point counts.

value.rationale: This is a natural good-reduction problem at the smallest odd prime dividing the automorphism-group order of the distinguished genus-four Bring curve. The familiar power-sum integral equations collapse at three; an explicit smooth elementary-symmetric alternative is geometrically informative. Its exact zeta and ordinarity provide a complete arithmetic description of the reduction, including a nontrivial point-free ordinary genus-four example. The isogeny premise is acknowledged as old, but good reduction of the curve is not an automatic consequence.
